overview: "Architecture-level repair of owner sign-in: separate Supabase authentication from IVX owner authorization, add per-stage timeouts, trace IDs, canonical state machine, and end-to-end production certification."

# Owner Authentication Hardening Plan

## 1. Evidence Gate (completed)

- Owner sign-in screen: `expo/app/login.tsx`
- Supabase client: `expo/lib/supabase.ts` (singleton with AsyncStorage adapter, custom fetch)
- signInWithPassword wrapper: `expo/lib/auth-password-sign-in.ts` (45s Promise.race — to be removed)
- Auth context: `expo/lib/auth-context.tsx` (login, handleSession, role resolution, trusted-device recovery)
- Auth store: `expo/lib/auth-store.ts` (token/userId/role persistence)
- Backend login: `backend/api/ivx-members.ts` → `backend/services/ivx-member-database.ts` (30s Promise.race — to be removed)
- Backend auth validation: `backend/api/ivx-members.ts` `requireAuthenticatedMember` (creates fresh anon client each call)
- Session storage: `AsyncStorage` via custom adapter in `expo/lib/supabase.ts` (chosen because JWT payloads exceed SecureStore Android limit)
- Auth-state listener: `expo/lib/auth-context.tsx` (single subscription, lightweight)
- Owner recovery: `expo/lib/auth-context.tsx` `restoreTrustedOwnerSession` / `activateOwnerIPSession` — trusted-device/IP subnet restore within 30-day window. **Will be hardened to require valid Supabase session or password re-entry.**
- Navigation after login: `expo/app/login.tsx` `navigateAfterSuccessfulLogin`
- Remember Me: UI checkbox in `expo/app/login.tsx` — currently only controls persisted session preference, no bypass. **Will be simplified/audited.**

## 2. Root Cause Hypothesis

The 30-second “Supabase Auth sign-in timed out” UX is produced by:
- A global `Promise.race([signInWithPassword(), timeout(30s)])` on the backend AND a 45s global wrapper on the mobile side.
- The UI is blocked until `handleSession()` completes role resolution (2.5s timeout + background hydration) before navigation.
- On cellular networks, the real Supabase Auth request can take 5–25s; combined with the UI blocking, it appears to hang for 30s.
- Error mapping is poor: any service failure returns “Aborted” / “Supabase Auth timed out”.

## 3. Target Architecture

```
IVX CLIENT
  ↓  (1) signInWithPassword directly to Supabase Auth — 8s hard timeout
SUPABASE AUTH
  ↓  (2) valid Supabase Session / JWT
IVX CLIENT
  ↓  (3) install session via setSession (automatic), persist to AsyncStorage
  ↓  (4) POST /api/ivx/owner/authorize with Bearer <JWT> — 6s timeout
IVX BACKEND
  ↓  (5) validate JWT with Supabase getUser, fetch owner profile/role
  ↓  (6) return { authorized, role, userId, email, expiresAt }
IVX CLIENT
  ↓  (7) set application session (user, role, isAuthenticated) and navigate
IVX APP
```

Authentication (WHO) is Supabase. Authorization (WHAT) is the IVX backend. No global timeout around the whole pipeline.

## 4. Changes

### Backend
- `backend/api/ivx-owner-auth.ts` (new): `POST /api/ivx/owner/authorize` validates the JWT with `client.auth.getUser(token)`, fetches profile from `profiles` with service role, and returns a canonical owner authorization result. No direct password handling here.
- `backend/api/ivx-members.ts`: remove 30s `Promise.race` from `loginMember` path; return structured Supabase errors immediately.
- `backend/api/ivx-members.ts`: `requireAuthenticatedMember` will use a single shared Supabase anon client (or `getUser` directly via `createClient` with no timeout) instead of creating a new client per request.

### Mobile
- `expo/lib/auth-password-sign-in.ts`: rewrite as thin `signInWithPassword` wrapper with no global timeout; only surface Supabase errors accurately.
- `expo/lib/auth-context.tsx`:
  - `login()` reverts to direct `signInWithPassword`.
  - Adds `authorizeOwner(session)` that calls `/api/ivx/owner/authorize` with 6s timeout.
  - `handleSession()` becomes non-blocking: install session, set optimistic role from backend response, navigate, then do background hydration.
  - Removes trusted-device IP/session activation that bypasses authentication. Trusted-device restore can only restore a valid persisted Supabase session (refresh token), not create an owner session from metadata alone.
  - `manualOwnerLoginRef` logic remains to prevent auto-login on manual sign-in.
- `expo/app/login.tsx`: implement canonical state machine (`idle`, `authenticating`, `session_ready`, `authorizing_owner`, `ready`, `failed`, `cancelled`) and derive all UI from it. Disable duplicate submission. Clear password after success.
- `expo/lib/supabase.ts`: reduce custom auth fetch timeout to 8s (auth network), keep 15s for REST, no global abort across the whole login flow.
- `expo/lib/auth-store.ts`: audit storage writes, ensure corrupted session returns to login.
- Add `expo/lib/login-trace.ts`: traceId generation, checkpoint logging (T1–T7) with no secrets.

### Tests
- `expo/__tests__/owner-auth-hardening.test.ts`: 18 required scenarios.
- `backend/tests/ivx-owner-auth.test.ts`: backend authorization scenarios.

## 5. Performance Targets

- T1 (tap → Supabase request start): <200ms
- T2 (Supabase request start → response): p95 <8s, target median <3s on Wi-Fi, <5s on cellular
- T3 (response → session persisted): <500ms
- T4-T6 (owner lookup/authorization): <6s total
- T7 (authorization → navigation complete): <500ms
- **Total login: <5s target on Wi-Fi, <8s on cellular.**

## 6. Security Hardening

- No plaintext password logging.
- No JWT/refresh token logging.
- Owner role decided by backend `profiles.role` + `verify_admin_access`, not client email allow-list.
- Remove email-allow-list fallback that promotes role to owner in `auth-context.tsx`.
- Trusted-device recovery requires a valid refreshable Supabase session.
- Logout clears all SecureStore/AsyncStorage auth keys and owner-trusted-device keys.

## 7. Deployment

- Commit to `main` via Git Data API.
- Deploy backend to Render.
- Build Android APK v1.10.2 (versionCode 100).
- Verify production SHA parity.
- Provide APK download link.

## 8. Final Certification

- Return the 30-row PASS/FAIL matrix from the owner directive.
- Return root cause, timing breakdown, architecture before/after, files changed, security changes, test results, network tests, GitHub/Deploy/Production QA, previous certificate gap, and remaining failures.

**Verdict until certified:** NOT END-TO-END COMPLETE.
